role.altitude: Her week is still directing aides, reading the referral, setting goals with the patient, and explaining the risks in the room. She stops hunting a referral when the fields are stored, stops retyping a goals note she has accepted, and stops reassembling a protocol paragraph that is already stored.
skills_to_grow: Watch an aide's hands and stop an unsafe exercise
Read a referral passage the list does not quote
Reject a goals draft that omits the reevaluation
Explain a risk the protocol paragraph does not state
role.ambitious_version: She still directs, decides the treatment, sets the goals and tells the patient. A blank referral field is read from the paper, and a protocol without a paragraph is explained by her.

tasks.short: Direct, supervise, assess, and talk with aides.

steps.what: List aide name, patient name and session start.
Direct and supervise the supportive personnel on these exercises.
Watch the supportive personnel perform the exercises.
Assess whether their technique is safe for this patient.
Communicate the next change to the supportive personnel.

tasks.design: The {CALENDAR} lists aide name, patient name and session start only when those fields are stored. She still directs, supervises, watches, assesses and tells the aide what to change. The list does not supervise, and nothing sends an alert.
tasks.previous_blocker: The assignment lived on a paper rota or in someone's head, so she asked who was in the room before she could direct the session.
tasks.enabler_now: A calendar row can show the aide, the patient and the start time when those were entered at booking. That is a list, not supervision.
tasks.still_hard: She has to see the hands and hear how the aide cues the patient. A blank aide name or a swapped patient still means she sorts the room herself.
tasks.human_edge: She is the person who can stop an unsafe exercise and show the aide the change while the patient is there.
tasks.altitude: She stops asking who was booked when the row is filled. Directing, supervising, assessing and the correction stay with her.

reach.task: Direct supportive personnel on activities of daily living for the same patient.
reach.learn: Which exercises overlap, so the two sessions do not give the aide contradictory instructions.

evidence.claim: The range is a scenario for a supervision session, not a published percentage. A filled calendar row only removes the hunt for who is booked. Model knowledge.

assumptions: Session fields are aide name, patient name and session start. The producer is whoever booked the session before this task. That capture is outside this task and is not counted as time saved.
If aide name, patient name or session start is blank, the list omits the row and she sorts the room herself. The list is not a score of the aide's work.
Directing, supervising, watching, assessing and telling the aide stay at full time. The only shortened step is finding the booking.
Nothing sends an alert and nothing messages the aide. Upkeep is 0.2 hours per 100 baseline hours of this task, for a wrong aide name she corrects before she directs.
unknowns: What share of sessions have aide name, patient name and start time stored before she walks in.
research_questions: On a sample of sessions, how often is the aide named on the booking rather than arranged in the room?

incremental.description: Correct a wrong aide name on the booking before she directs the session.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a session where aide, patient and start are filled, she skips the hunt for the booking. On a blank row, or a session that is all watching and correcting, the saving is near zero. Directing, supervising, assessing and the spoken correction are not shortened.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review the referral and determine the treatment.

steps.what: List the physician referral reason, diagnosis and precautions.
Review the medical records the referral points to.
Determine the physical therapy treatment required for this diagnosis.
Write the treatment required on this patient's plan line.

tasks.design: The patient record in {OTHER} lists referral reason, diagnosis and precautions only when those fields are stored. She still reviews the records, determines the physical therapy treatment, and writes the plan line herself. The list does not determine the treatment, and nothing sends an alert.
tasks.previous_blocker: The referral arrived as a letter or a scanned note, and she paged the chart to find the reason and the precautions.
tasks.enabler_now: A record can show reason, diagnosis and precautions when the referral was entered as fields. The reading and the treatment decision stay hers.
tasks.still_hard: A narrative referral still has to be read. The diagnosis on the referral is not yet the treatment she will give.
tasks.human_edge: She judges which findings in the record change the treatment, including precautions a list can show but not weigh.
tasks.altitude: She stops paging for a referral that is already filed as fields. Reviewing the record and determining the treatment stay with her.

reach.task: Write the referral that states the diagnosis and the precautions.
reach.learn: Which of reason, diagnosis and precautions must be filled, or she reads the paper referral and the list stays blank.

evidence.claim: The dossier is kept twenty years after the last change. She writes the plan line into that record. She does not make a second archive.
Solely automated decisions about care need a basis in the privacy rule on automated decisions. The list does not determine the diagnosis or the physical therapy treatment.
The range is a scenario for finding a referral, not a published percentage. Model knowledge.

assumptions: Referral fields are reason, diagnosis text and precautions. The producer is the referring physician, or the person who entered that referral before this task. That capture is outside this task and is not counted as time saved.
If reason, diagnosis or precautions is blank, the list omits it and she reads the paper referral. The list does not invent a diagnosis.
Reviewing the records, determining the treatment and writing the plan line stay at full time. The only shortened step is the hunt for those three fields.
Nothing sends the plan line onward and nothing raises an alert. Upkeep is 0.3 hours per 100 baseline hours of this task, for a precaution row that names the wrong patient and has to be set aside.
unknowns: What share of referrals arrive with reason, diagnosis and precautions already stored as fields.
research_questions: On a sample of new courses, how often is the referral a structured row rather than a letter?

incremental.description: Set aside a precaution row that names the wrong patient before she determines treatment.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a referral where reason, diagnosis and precautions are filled, she skips paging for those three fields. On a letter, a blank precaution, or a record she must read in full, the saving is near zero. Determining the treatment and writing the plan line are not shortened.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Set goals, progress and the reevaluation plan.

steps.what: Identify the goals, anticipated progress and reevaluation plan.
Agree those goals and that progress with the patient.
Draft the note that will document those goals and that progress.

loop.input: the goals, the anticipated progress and the reevaluation plan she stated
loop.check: she checks that the draft states those goals and that reevaluation plan, not only the patient id
loop.stop: one draft, then stop; if she rejects it she writes the note herself
loop.why_not_simpler: the goals are her words from the room, so a fixed form cannot draft the note

steps.what: Check the draft states the goals and the reevaluation plan.
File the confirmed goals and reevaluation plans.

tasks.design: A draft note in {OTHER} is produced from the goals, the anticipated progress and the reevaluation plan she has just stated. She checks that the draft states those goals and that plan, and only that confirmed version is filed. The draft does not set the goals, and nothing sends an alert.
tasks.previous_blocker: She retyped the goals after the conversation, often from memory, into the record.
tasks.enabler_now: A scribe can draft from what she said, and she can accept or reject that draft before anything is filed. The goals themselves are still hers.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing a goal the patient can actually meet, and saying it in the room, does not get shorter. A rejected draft is written by her.
tasks.human_edge: She chooses the goal and hears whether the patient can live with it. The draft cannot do that conversation.
tasks.altitude: She stops retyping a goals note she has accepted. Identifying the goals and agreeing them with the patient stay with her.

reach.task: Document functional goals for the same patient.
reach.learn: Which goal lines the two plans share, so the same goal is not written twice with two dates.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber records the consultation, the clinician validates, and the note goes into HiX, Nedap ONS or Nexus. It claims 15 to 20 minutes saved per consult, with no method given. That figure is not the saving on this goals task.
Tandem's scribe and coding carry MDR class IIa. The draft here is a goals note she validates before filing. It does not code the visit and it does not set the goal.

At Capio Ramsay Santé, self-estimated time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes across 236,153 Tandem notes, and median editing stayed 93 seconds. Three of seven authors are from the vendor. Those are note minutes, not the time to identify and agree a goal.
Providers stay legally responsible for careful use of generative AI, including the risk of a wrong registration. She checks the goals text before it is filed.
AI that needs a notified body is high-risk from 2 August 2028, and Annex III duties apply from 2 December 2027. This draft does not decide eligibility for care and it does not triage.
The dossier is kept twenty years after the last change. The filed plan stays in that dossier. She does not keep a second archive.
Solely automated decisions about care need a basis in the privacy rule on automated decisions. The draft does not choose the goals or the reevaluation date.
Ambient recording can be a facility that monitors staff performance, so the works council must consent. The draft listens to the goals she states. It is not a score of her work.
The range is a scenario for the note, not the published note-time percentage and not the whole goal-setting visit. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The draft uses only the goals, the anticipated progress and the reevaluation plan she stated in the room. It does not pull a goal from another patient.
If she rejects the draft, she writes the note herself and that time is the incremental allowance, not a saving.
Identifying the goals and agreeing them with the patient stay at full time. The shortened steps are the draft and the filing of the version she accepted.
Filing writes only goals-plan-v1, the version she checked. A later edit voids that acceptance and is a new write.
Nothing sends the plan and nothing raises an alert. The dossier retention stays in the record. No second archive step.

Reading the draft for a missing goal or a missing reevaluation plan is already in the check step. Upkeep beyond that is 0.4 hours per 100 baseline hours of this task, for a draft that names the wrong patient and must be discarded.
unknowns: Whether this clinic already allows a scribe to listen in the treatment room.
How often she rejects the draft and types the goals herself.
research_questions: On a sample of new plans, how often does the accepted note match what she said, without a rewrite?

already_counted.description: Read the draft for a missing goal or a missing reevaluation plan.

incremental.description: Discard a draft that names the wrong patient and write the goals herself.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a plan where she accepts the draft, she skips retyping the goals and the reevaluation plan. On a rejected draft, or a visit that is mostly agreeing the goals in the room, the saving is near zero. Identifying the goals and agreeing them are not shortened. The figure is not the published note-time percentage.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Decide the proposed intervention for this patient.
Draft the risks, benefits and alternatives from the cited paragraph.

loop.input: the stored protocol paragraph for the intervention she named
loop.output: draft explanation of risks, benefits and alternatives
loop.check: she checks that the draft names those risks and benefits and does not add a risk the paragraph does not state
loop.stop: one draft, then stop; if the paragraph is missing or she rejects it she explains without a draft
loop.why_not_simpler: the paragraph is prose, so copying the whole protocol would not separate risks, benefits and alternatives

steps.what: Check the draft names the risks and benefits of this intervention.
Provide information on the material risks, expected benefits and reasonable alternatives.

tasks.design: A draft in {DOCS} quotes only a stored protocol paragraph for the intervention she has already named, and only when that paragraph is stored. She checks that it names the risks and benefits and adds none the paragraph does not state. She then tells the patient herself. The draft does not speak to the patient, and nothing sends a message or an alert.
tasks.previous_blocker: The risks and alternatives sat in a long protocol, and she reassembled them from memory before the conversation.
tasks.enabler_now: A draft can separate risks, benefits and alternatives from one stored paragraph. The conversation with the patient stays hers.
tasks.still_hard: She still has to say it, hear the patient's questions, and judge an alternative the paragraph does not fit. A missing paragraph means there is no draft.
tasks.human_edge: She tells this patient, in the room, which risks matter for this intervention and which alternative is reasonable.
tasks.altitude: She stops reassembling a protocol paragraph that is already stored. Deciding the intervention and telling the patient stay with her.

reach.task: Explain the medical risks of the condition that led to the referral.
reach.learn: Which risks stay with the physician, and which risks of the exercise she must say herself.

evidence.claim: Thuisarts is guideline-based information from NHG, FMS and Patiëntenfederatie. It is an example of a vetted text. This draft quotes a protocol paragraph stored locally. It does not claim that Thuisarts holds this clinic's exercise risks.
Providers stay legally responsible for careful use of generative AI. She checks that the draft does not add a risk the paragraph does not state, and she speaks the explanation herself.
Solely automated decisions about care need a basis in the privacy rule on automated decisions. The draft does not choose the intervention or the alternative.
The range is a scenario for preparing the explanation, not a published percentage, and not the conversation itself. Model knowledge.

assumptions: Protocol fields are protocol name, paragraph id and paragraph text. The producer is the person who approved that protocol into the document store before this task. That capture is outside this task and is not counted as time saved.
If the paragraph is missing, or it is not about the intervention she named, the draft does not run and she explains without it. The draft does not invent a risk.
Deciding the intervention and telling the patient stay at full time. The only shortened step is separating risks, benefits and alternatives from a stored paragraph.
The draft is not sent to the patient and it is not a chatbot. Nothing raises an alert. There is no sheet to fill.

Reading the draft for a risk the paragraph does not state is already in the check step. Upkeep is 0.3 hours per 100 baseline hours of this task, for a paragraph that was stored against the wrong intervention and has to be set aside.
unknowns: What share of this clinic's interventions have a stored paragraph that states risks, benefits and alternatives.
Whether patients already receive a paper sheet from the protocol, separate from this conversation.
research_questions: On a sample of new interventions, how often is there a stored paragraph she can quote before she speaks?

already_counted.description: Read the draft for a risk the paragraph does not state.

incremental.description: Set aside a paragraph stored against the wrong intervention.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a visit where the protocol paragraph is stored and she keeps the draft, she skips reassembling that paragraph. On a missing paragraph, a rejected draft, or a visit that is the conversation itself, the saving is near zero. Deciding the intervention and telling the patient are not shortened.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
